title: Keep shared loss separate from per-link service survival
statement: If every one-hit connection in a region requires the same association to survive, and that association delaminates with probability delta, chemistry alone cannot exceed1-delta regional success. Under an independent contact-first gate p_c=g/(g+d), the ceiling is p_c*(1-delta); for M independent identical regions all-success is at most[p_c*(1-delta)]^M. More one-hit candidates cannot remove this shared-loss ceiling.

requires: One shared mechanical association is necessary for all candidate one-hit paths in the region.
The contact/delamination product requires independence or an explicit conditional loss law; the M-region product additionally requires independent regions.
provides: If every one-hit connection in a region requires the same association to survive, and that association delaminates with probability delta, chemistry alone cannot exceed1-delta regional success. Under an independent contact-first gate p_c=g/(g+d), the ceiling is p_c*(1-delta); for M independent identical regions all-success is at most[p_c*(1-delta)]^M. assumptions: A shared loss is not independent per-link thinning. Correlation with contact or a distinct surviving backup changes the product/ceiling.
Only the elementary stated ceiling is internally verified here; the reported hybrid optimization and stochastic check lack their governing original.
costs: Extra candidates pay supply without overcoming an unchanged shared gate. A backup pays real independent load paths, material and mechanical qualification.
contract.units: delta,p_c and success are dimensionless probabilities; M counts independent regions; g,d share one inverse-time unit.
contract.obstruction: Acquire the association-loss law and genuinely distinct backup support; preserve the missing hybrid-proof/code gap.

body: On the shared loss event every dependent one-hit load path fails, even if all grafts form. Intersect surviving association with required contact; the product requires independence (or a correctly calibrated conditional loss probability). Cross-region powers require independent regions. Independent per-link survival S instead thins the candidate count and is not the same model. A two-sided backup could evade this particular loss only if its load path and failure are actually distinct; the unavailable hybrid helper and reported221-versus332 reaction-site optimum do not establish that interface or optimum here. No missing code or whole hybrid model is reconstructed from its attractive summary.

evidence.range_scope: Elementary shared-delamination/contact ceiling; excludes the later unsupported hybrid optimization.
evidence.quote: ## 4. A surprising result: two different welding chemistries can outperform either alone
evidence.status: Exact frozen source bytes; scientific acceptance is scoped to actual version-bound review.

review.scope: Completed source-exposed author reconstruction of uniform-window Poisson integration at k=d, the incomplete-gamma fixed-m expression and m/X tail, the one-hit small-time rate change, shared-anchor/contact ceiling under explicit independence, and conditional single-end mass accounting. New scientific response and the available original code were fully read statically, not executed. Earlier accepted two-hit units remain unchanged. The missing hybrid helper prevents acceptance of the reported optimum/Monte Carlo; cited primary studies, AFM-to-strength transfer, actual kinetics and physical welding/regeneration are not newly validated.
